<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="טבת_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518916295_theRebbe_70" batchId="meluket-_D7_98_D7_91_D7_AA_meluket__BH_POST_1766518916295_theRebbe_70__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Though Torah makes a dwelling for G-d, the aspect of "one is she" is needed to connect Torah with its Giver, achieved through prayer which begins with the contemplation of "your eyes are doves," gathering all one's faculties to receive from the One, culminating in self-sacrifice, thereby perfecting the divine desire for a dwelling and making one a partner with G-d.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And behold, even though through this</t>
    <t s="1">(the matter of Torah)</t>
    <t s="2">a dwelling place is made for Him, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="3">there must be the aspect of "one is she,"</t>
    <t s="4">in order to connect the Torah with the Giver of the Torah,</t>
    <t s="5">which is achieved through His having chosen us from all the nations and given us His Torah,</t>
    <t s="6">for then "the L-rd is with him, that the law is according to him in every place,"</t>
    <t s="7">behold, for this the service of prayer is needed, through which the aspect of "one" is achieved,</t>
    <t s="8">that he receives from the One.</t>
    <t s="9">For the beginning of the service of prayer is the aspect of "my dove,"</t>
    <t s="10">which is as it is written,</t>
    <t s="11">"Your eyes are doves,"</t>
    <t s="12">and this is the contemplation</t>
    <t s="13">(hear)</t>
    <t s="14">and the looking in the Shema that precedes prayer</t>
    <t s="15">(the Silent Prayer),</t>
    <t s="16">and even before that, in the blessings of the Shema and in Pesukei DeZimra, where one contemplates and looks, which is the matter of "your eyes are doves," etc.,</t>
    <t s="17">until it reaches "Hear O Israel, the L-rd our G-d, the L-rd is One,"</t>
    <t s="18">for "Shema" is also an expression of gathering and collecting,</t>
    <t s="19">that he gathers all his affairs,</t>
    <t s="20">and becomes a receiver from the L-rd our G-d,</t>
    <t s="21">which is the aspect of "one," and until he reaches the aspect of "with all your might,"</t>
    <t s="22">which is the matter of self-sacrifice.</t>
    <t s="23">And through the service of "one is she, my dove,"</t>
    <t s="24">there is achieved "my perfect one," from the term of perfection and completeness, which effects completeness,</t>
    <t s="25">filling and completing the will and desire that the Holy One, blessed be He, desired to have a dwelling place for Himself, blessed be He, in the lower realms,</t>
    <t s="26">which is through the Torah, through which He effects in the world all the matters mentioned above.</t>
    <t s="27">And also the second interpretation of "my perfect one,"</t>
    <t s="28">"my twin,"</t>
    <t s="29">that he becomes a partner with the Holy One, blessed be He, in the act of Creation,</t>
    <t s="30">(and all the explanations explained in the discourses on the verse in Torah Ohr</t>
    <t s="31">and in Likkutei Torah on Song of Songs</t>
    <t s="32">of the Baal HaHilula).</t>
    <t s="33">And he concludes, "One is she, my dove, my perfect one, she is the only one of her mother," as explained in the aforementioned discourses.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The exile in Egypt was like an iron furnace to refine the world to receive the Torah, and just as prayer (the aspect of "one is she") precedes and connects Torah to G-d, so too the revelation of "I am the L-rd" through Torah must be preceded by the service of the Patriarchs who instituted the prayers.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And this is the meaning of what is written, "And G-d spoke to Moshe and said to him, 'I am the L-rd,'"</t>
    <t s="1">for behold, the exile of Egypt was analogous to an iron furnace,</t>
    <t s="2">for in order that the world could receive the Torah, and study leading to deed,</t>
    <t s="3">the matter of the commandments,</t>
    <t s="4">it was necessary to precede it with "and they embittered their lives and they worked them"</t>
    <t s="5">"the children of Israel with rigor,"</t>
    <t s="6">which is the clarification and refinement accomplished through the iron furnace,</t>
    <t s="7">which prepared the world to receive the Torah.</t>
    <t s="8">This is not so in the time of the Patriarchs before the exile of Egypt,</t>
    <t s="9">when the world was not yet prepared, etc.</t>
    <t s="10">And through the Torah, the truth of the L-rd is drawn into the world,</t>
    <t s="11">for the Torah, called "the Torah of the L-rd," acts upon "In the beginning G-d created"</t>
    <t s="12">so that it will be in ultimate perfection,</t>
    <t s="13">analogous to what was explained above regarding "my perfect one," that the supernal will that existed at the creation of the world is completed,</t>
    <t s="14">"In the beginning" for the sake of the Torah, which is called "beginning."</t>
    <t s="15">However, as explained above, that even though the drawing of the dwelling place in the lower realms is through "sixty are queens and eighty concubines and maidens without number,"</t>
    <t s="16">the matter of Torah,</t>
    <t s="17">there must precede this the matter of prayer, the aspect of "one is she, my dove,"</t>
    <t s="18">through which the connection of Israel with the Holy One, blessed be He, is made,</t>
    <t s="19">and afterwards, and through this, Israel acts upon the Torah, which becomes connected with the Holy One, blessed be He, and then it draws from above downward.</t>
    <t s="20">And as is known</t>
    <t s="21">one of the explanations in the statement of our sages, of blessed memory,</t>
    <t s="22">"Three knots are tied one to another: Israel, the Torah, and the Holy One, blessed be He,"</t>
    <t s="23">for at first glance, in a connection of three things there are only two connections,</t>
    <t s="24">rather, Israel is also connected to the Holy One, blessed be He, in a direct manner,</t>
    <t s="25">and as it is in a circle.</t>
    <t s="26">For the connection is not only from above downward,</t>
    <t s="27">that the Holy One, blessed be He, is above, and below that is the Torah,</t>
    <t s="28">and below that is Israel,</t>
    <t s="29">but rather, Israel themselves are also connected to the Holy One, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="30">and through this, they draw from the Holy One, blessed be He, into the Torah, analogous to what is explained, that Dovid would connect the Torah with the Holy One, blessed be He.</t>
    <t s="31">Behold, just as through the aspect of "one is she, my dove," which is the matter of prayer,</t>
    <t s="32">they effect the connection of the Torah with the Holy One, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="33">so too is it regarding the matter of "I am the L-rd,"</t>
    <t s="34">which is the matter of the Torah, which is the true essence of Himself, "Me you are taking"</t>
    <t s="35">through the Torah,</t>
    <t s="36">for the innerness of Abba is the innerness of Atik,</t>
    <t s="37">which is Essence and Being,</t>
    <t s="38">behold, before this there must be "And I appeared to Avraham, to Yitzchak, and to Yaakov,"</t>
    <t s="39">which is the matter of prayer,</t>
    <t s="40">for the Patriarchs instituted the prayers,</t>
    <t s="41">and in particular,</t>
    <t s="42">Avraham, Yitzchak, and Yaakov are the three prayers of Shacharit, Minchah, and Maariv,</t>
    <t s="43">which was the preparation for the service of the children, for "the deeds of the Patriarchs are a sign for the children."</t>
    <t s="44">For there must be both matters of Torah and prayer.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>When Israel needed to leave Egypt, the aspect of judgment (Elokim) was still revealed, but through the prayer of the Patriarchs (the aspect of "one is she"), the revelation of "I am the L-rd" was drawn via Moshe, bringing the redemption from concealment and Egypt, culminating in the entry to the good and broad land with the coming of Moshiach.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And this is the meaning of "And G-d spoke," etc.,</t>
    <t s="1">for when Israel needed to leave the exile of Egypt, the aspect of Gevurah was still revealed, which is the matter of the name Elokim.</t>
    <t s="2">And like Pharaoh who said, "I do not know the L-rd,"</t>
    <t s="3">that he is not connected to the name Havayah,</t>
    <t s="4">for his matter and root is that he suckles from the forty-eight final permutations of the name Elokim,</t>
    <t s="5">and therefore also among Israel,</t>
    <t s="6">with due distinction,</t>
    <t s="7">who were then in the exile of Egypt, it was also in such a manner.</t>
    <t s="8">But afterwards, "And G-d spoke to Moshe and said to him, 'I am the L-rd,'"</t>
    <t s="9">that the time had come for the aspect of "I am the L-rd" to be revealed,</t>
    <t s="10">and it is through the preface of "And I appeared to Avraham, to Yitzchak, and to Yaakov,"</t>
    <t s="11">which is the matter of prayer, as above,</t>
    <t s="12">the aspect of "one is she, my dove,"</t>
    <t s="13">for from the perspective of this aspect, it is not appropriate to have misgivings about His attributes, and as our sages, of blessed memory, said,</t>
    <t s="14">"With all your might" — with every measure that He measures out to you,</t>
    <t s="15">and afterwards, and through this, the aspect of "I am the L-rd" is drawn,</t>
    <t s="16">and it is drawn through Moshe, as it is written, "Therefore say to the children of Israel, 'I am the L-rd,'"</t>
    <t s="17">"Moshe received the Torah from Sinai and transmitted it," etc.,</t>
    <t s="18">the giving of the Torah to Israel, through which the name Havayah will be revealed,</t>
    <t s="19">that the Ten Commandments will be drawn into the Ten Utterances with which the world was created,</t>
    <t s="20">redemption from concealment and from Egypt, and with all four expressions of redemption: "and I will take you out, and I will rescue you, and I will redeem you, and I will take you," and until "and I will bring you"</t>
    <t s="21">"to a good land"</t>
    <t s="22">(the opposite of concealment)</t>
    <t s="23">"and broad"</t>
    <t s="24">(the opposite of Egypt)</t>
    <t s="25">speedily, literally, in our times, through Moshiach our righteous one.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
